messages.content: I have a new audit in Durham. The opening meeting is Tuesday, June 17 at 8:30 a.m., and we should finish the closing meeting by 4:00 Thursday. I can travel Monday. Please compare coming home Thursday night with staying until Friday, including flights, hotel, and transportation.
I can build both versions. Which Durham location should I use for hotel and drive-time estimates, and is there a required arrival time on Monday?
The laboratory is near TW Alexander Drive and Miami Boulevard. There is no Monday commitment, but I need enough time to check in, eat, and be ready for an early start Tuesday. Departure is from SFO.

For Monday, June 16, the best two one-stop choices are a United itinerary through Denver, departing SFO at 8:20 a.m. and reaching RDU at 6:18 p.m., with 6 hours 58 minutes elapsed travel time, and a Delta itinerary through Atlanta, departing at 7:05 a.m. and arriving at 5:27 p.m., with 7 hours 22 minutes elapsed. The Delta connection is longer but gets you in 51 minutes earlier. I’ll compare each against the Thursday and Friday returns. Do you need a checked bag included?
Yes, include one checked bag. The earlier arrival Monday is more useful unless it makes the total unreasonable.

With one checked bag, the Delta round trip returning Thursday is $612. The outbound is SFO 7:05 a.m.-ATL 2:47 p.m., then ATL 4:05 p.m.-RDU 5:27 p.m. The latest workable Thursday return is RDU 6:35 p.m.-CLT 7:42 p.m., then CLT 8:35 p.m.-SFO 11:14 p.m.; total return travel time is 7 hours 39 minutes. That departure leaves little margin after a 4:00 p.m. closing meeting. A Friday return using the same Delta outbound is $548 including the bag: RDU 9:10 a.m.-ATL 10:37 a.m., then ATL 12:05 p.m.-SFO 2:24 p.m., 8 hours 14 minutes elapsed.
Quantify the Thursday risk. Assume the meeting really ends at 4:00, not earlier.

From the lab area to RDU, the normal drive is about 15-20 minutes, but weekday traffic and terminal access can push it to 30 minutes. Leaving the site at 4:10 after packing up would likely put you at the terminal between 4:30 and 4:45. The checked-bag cutoff for a 6:35 departure is expected to be 5:50, leaving 65-80 minutes before that cutoff. A meeting overrun of 30 minutes, heavier traffic, or time spent waiting for a rideshare would materially narrow the margin. It is possible, but not robust.
Check whether there is anything later Thursday. I do not want to assume that 6:35 is the only choice.

There is a 7:12 p.m. United departure through Washington Dulles, arriving SFO at 12:18 a.m. Friday. It costs $731 round trip with the bag and takes 8 hours 6 minutes on the return. That adds 37 minutes of airport margin but costs $119 more than the 6:35 option and arrives after midnight. There is also an 8:05 p.m. itinerary, but it has an overnight connection and does not reach SFO until 8:42 a.m. Friday, so it offers no practical advantage over a Durham hotel night.
Agreed. Use the 6:35 flight for the Thursday version and the 9:10 flight for Friday. Now look at practical hotels close to the laboratory, not downtown Durham.

Three suitable options near Research Triangle Park are: Home2 Suites Raleigh Durham Airport RTP, about 4 miles from the lab area, at an estimated $168 per night including tax and breakfast; Delta Hotels Raleigh-Durham at Research Triangle Park, about 3 miles away, at $176 including tax, with an on-site restaurant and airport shuttle; and Marriott Raleigh Durham Research Triangle Park, about 2 miles away, at $194 including tax, also with an on-site restaurant. All three include Wi-Fi. The Delta is the strongest practical middle option because it is close, has dinner on site, and can cover the airport transfer during shuttle hours.
Does the Delta shuttle run early enough for the Friday flight, and can it be reserved?

The published shuttle hours are 5:00 a.m. to midnight, and the hotel recommends arranging the airport trip with the front desk the night before. For a 9:10 a.m. departure with a checked bag, a 6:45 a.m. shuttle request would be appropriate. The shuttle is complimentary, but timing is not guaranteed until the hotel confirms the request at check-in.
Keep the shuttle out of the cost comparison, then. Price rideshares for everything so authorization does not depend on it.

Using rideshares throughout, I estimate $32 each way between RDU and the hotel, including a moderate surge allowance, and $25 each way between the Delta hotel and the laboratory. Airport transfers total $64. Six hotel-site trips across Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday total $150, so the working transportation estimate is $214 for either itinerary. If the hotel shuttle is available, the actual total could be lower.
Would a rental car be cheaper? Include parking and fuel, and check whether the hotel charges for parking.

The Delta hotel lists complimentary self-parking. A compact rental picked up Monday evening and returned Thursday would be about $268 including taxes, plus roughly $30 for fuel, or $298 total. Returning Friday raises the rental estimate to $326, plus $30 fuel, or $356. Rideshares are therefore about $84 less for the Thursday plan and $142 less for the Friday plan. The rental gives more control on Thursday, but it does not remove the risk from a late closing meeting.
Use rideshares. Please give me complete totals for the Delta hotel, and also show how much more Friday costs despite the lower airfare.

Monday-through-Thursday: airfare $612, three hotel nights at $176 for $528, and estimated rideshares $214, totaling $1,354. Monday-through-Friday: airfare $548, four hotel nights at $176 for $704, and estimated rideshares $214, totaling $1,466. Staying Friday costs $112 more overall. The $64 airfare saving offsets part of the extra $176 hotel night.
Are those hotel numbers fully loaded? I need the authorization request to include tax and any mandatory destination or parking fees.

Yes. The $176 nightly estimate includes the currently displayed room rate, occupancy taxes, and mandatory hotel charges. Self-parking is complimentary, and no destination fee is listed. The three-night lodging estimate is $528 and the four-night estimate is $704. Meals and incidental holds are not included.
Put the schedules side by side in prose, including when I would likely reach the hotel Monday and when I would leave it Friday.

Both plans begin Monday, June 16 with Delta departing SFO at 7:05 a.m., connecting in Atlanta, and arriving RDU at 5:27 p.m. Allowing for the checked bag and rideshare pickup, you would likely reach the Delta hotel around 6:30-6:45 p.m. The Thursday plan has the audit Tuesday through Thursday, then a target departure from the lab no later than 4:10 p.m. for the 6:35 p.m. flight through Charlotte, arriving SFO at 11:14 p.m. The Friday plan returns to the hotel after Thursday’s close, adds a fourth night, and leaves the hotel around 6:45 a.m. Friday for the 9:10 a.m. flight through Atlanta, arriving SFO at 2:24 p.m.
Prepare the authorization recommendation for the Friday plan, but retain the Thursday plan as the lower-cost alternative. Do not book anything yet.

Authorization recommendation: Monday, June 16 through Friday, June 20, using the Delta one-stop outbound arriving RDU at 5:27 p.m., four nights at Delta Hotels Raleigh-Durham at Research Triangle Park, rideshares for airport and laboratory transportation, and the Friday 9:10 a.m. return arriving SFO at 2:24 p.m. Estimated total is $1,466: $548 airfare with one checked bag, $704 lodging including taxes and mandatory charges, and $214 ground transportation. Rationale: the extra hotel night avoids tying a 6:35 p.m. departure to a 4:00 p.m. closing meeting. Lower-cost alternative: return Thursday for $1,354, saving $112, with a target site departure by 4:10 p.m. No flights, hotel, or transportation have been booked.
